## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Parihānikathā* (Kv 1.2) is the second section of the first chapter (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The controversy addresses the pivotal question of whether an arahant can undergo retrogression or fall away (*arahā parihāyati* / *arahattā parihāni*) [Skorupski 1991; Waldron 2003]. According to the commentarial tradition, non-Theravāda groups such as the Sammatīyas, Vajjiputtiyas, Sabbatthivādins, and certain Mahāsaṅghikas maintained that an arahant could experience decline due to an eruption of passion (*rāgaparyuṭṭhita*) conditioned by latent underlying dispositions (*anusaya*); Theravāda debaters reject this, denying that fully liberated beings retain such dispositions [Waldron 2003].
SuttaCentral records that the discourse draws upon or references canonical passages found in the *Paṭhamasamayavimuttasutta* (AN 5.149), the *Dutiyasamayavimuttasutta* (AN 5.150), the *Soṇasutta* (AN 6.55), the *Cammakkhandhaka* (Kd 5), and the *Nālaka Sutta* (Snp 3.11) [SuttaCentral]. In DharmaNexus text-reuse computations, Kv 1.2 exhibits thousands of Pali-internal shared passages across the *Kathāvatthu*, most substantially with structurally parallel debates including the *Parūpahārakathā* (Kv 2.1), *Aññāṇakathā* (Kv 2.2), *Paravitāraṇakathā* (Kv 2.4), *Kaṅkhākathā* (Kv 2.3), and *Sabbamatthītikathā* (Kv 1.6), in addition to sharing segments with the *Pañcakanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 5) and the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of the text with Sanskrit and Tibetan works, including the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā*, Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra*, the *Śrāvakabhūmi*, and Candrakīrti's *Prasannapadā*, reflecting shared dialectical terminology and canonical phrasing [DharmaNexus].
